decision_rules: No cleanup, migration, deletion, mount creation, partition change or Docker reconfiguration may happen in R2.
R3 is blocked until the owner explicitly selects one option, the exact candidate list, the FAST_HOT quota and the reserve floor.
Every migration must be checksum-verified and must land on /data before any SSD source is removed.
If a selected metric or capacity cannot be measured, the result is EVIDENCE_INSUFFICIENT, not PASS.
If a FAST_HOT surface resolves to rotational storage, the result is CONTRACT_MISMATCH.
The S1 scientific manifest, seeds, reward, model, optimizer, budget, evaluation and thresholds are unchanged by this proposal.

reserve_floor_definition.meaning: Free bytes that must remain available on the SSD root filesystem after FAST_HOT allocation and before R3 proceeds.
reserve_floor_definition.note: Options below all keep at least this reserve unless the owner explicitly accepts a lower floor.

options.name: No cleanup - carve FAST_HOT from existing free SSD space
options.summary: Create FAST_HOT directly from the current 34.0 GB free root-LV space without deleting or migrating any data.
pros: No deletion and no data migration.
Preserves all current user and system data.
cons: SSD root stays above 93 percent after the reserve is reduced.
FAST_HOT capacity is limited to about 22 GiB.
Likely insufficient for 8-worker production-shaped formal scratch plus hot metadata.
Conflicts with the architecture direction to perform cleanup/provisioning first.

options.name: Safe reclaim - caches/logs/crash/apt/disabled snaps/conda cache
options.summary: Reclaim low-sensitivity caches and logs, then allocate a larger FAST_HOT while keeping a 20 GiB reserve.
pros: No user project or media migration is required.
Frees enough SSD space for a 44.7 GiB FAST_HOT with a 20 GiB reserve.
Conda package cache and uv/pip caches are re-creatable.
cons: Model/package caches may be re-downloaded later, consuming network/time.
Deleting conda package cache can slow environment rebuilds.
Crash dumps must be reviewed before deletion.
options.recommendation_note: Lowest-risk option that still creates meaningful FAST_HOT headroom.

options.name: Migrate selected cold media/audio data to HDD
options.summary: Copy and checksum-verify selected cold user data to /data, then remove the SSD copies to free about 86 GiB.
pros: No user data is deleted; it is moved to HDD with checksum proof.
Frees about 86 GiB of SSD space.
Supports a larger FAST_HOT and a larger reserve.
cons: Copy time and HDD I/O during migration.
Requires careful checksum and deletion proof.
Some applications may expect those paths to remain on the SSD.

options.name: Combined safe reclaim plus selected cold-data migration
options.summary: Apply option B and option C together to free about 119 GiB and allocate a 111.8 GiB FAST_HOT with a 38.9 GiB reserve.
pros: Largest available FAST_HOT capacity without new hardware.
Combines cache reclamation with checksum-verified cold-data migration.
cons: Most owner decisions and the longest execution path.
Combines the risks of option B and option C.
Requires a precise keep list and migration verification evidence.
options.recommendation_note: Recommended only if R4/R5 evidence indicates that 44.7 GiB FAST_HOT is insufficient.

options.name: Add a new SSD/NVMe device for FAST_HOT
options.summary: Provision an additional non-rotational device and allocate FAST_HOT there; no deletion or migration on the existing root LV.
options.reserve_floor_human: 31.69 GiB on existing root; new device must define its own reserve
pros: No existing user data needs deletion or migration.
Separates hot storage from the already-occupied root LV.
cons: Requires procurement and physical host access.
Long lead time and likely stronger host/power/thermal validation.
Not available for the immediate Recovery schedule.

not_recommended_explicit_exclusions.reason: Relocating or reducing the 32 GiB swapfile could free SSD space but risks host stability and swap behaviour; it is not part of any option above and requires a separate host decision.
HuggingFace cache is the largest single cache (40.9 GB) but may contain models needed offline; deleting it requires an owner-selected model list. It is not in the default options.

recommendation.default_reason: Frees about 33 GiB with low data-loss risk and creates a 44.7 GiB FAST_HOT plus a 20.2 GiB reserve.
recommendation.condition_for_larger_option: Choose D_COMBINED_RECLAIM_AND_MIGRATION only if R4/R5 measured evidence shows that 44.7 GiB FAST_HOT is insufficient or if the owner wants a larger reserve margin.
